Rashi on Shabbat 30b:10:1.english: [He] scoffed - This is [the] folly [referred to in the verse].

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:10:2.hebrew: צלף - מין אילן הטוען ג' מיני פירות: אביונות, וקפריסין, ולולבין. וכי איתיה להאי, ליתיה להאי, כדאמר בריש חזקת הבתים:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:10:2.english: A caper bush - A species of tree that bears three kinds of fruit: caper berries [evyonot], caper buds [kafrisin], and young shoots [lulavin]. And when this [one] is present, that [one] is not present, as [the Gemara] says at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Chezkot HaBatim.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:11:1.hebrew: בר - כמו ״לשבור בר״ (בראשית מב). ולענין כלי מילת — ״בר״ הוא נקי, כמו ״ברה כחמה״ (שיר ו):
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:11:1.english: Bar - [Regarding the cakes, it is] like “to purchase grain [bar]” (Genesis 42:3); and with regard to fine wool garments, bar [means] clean, like “pure [barah] as the sun” (Song of Songs 6:10).

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:11:2.hebrew: פיסת בר - משמע גלוסקאות, שרחבות כמין פס יד; ומשמע כלי מילת, כמו ״כתונת פסים״:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:11:2.english: Abundant grain - It implies fine loaves, which are as wide as the palm of a hand; and it implies garments of fine wool, like “a tunic of passim [ketonet passim].”

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:11:3.hebrew: כמהין ופטריות - שיוצאין כמות שהן בלילה אחד, ורחבין ועגולין כגלוסקאות:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:11:3.english: Truffles and mushrooms - For they emerge as they are in a single night, and are broad and round like cakes.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:11:4.hebrew: נברא בר קורא - סיב, כמין לבוש מצוייר, גדל סביבות הקור של דקל כשהוא רך. קור — ענף האילן כשהוא רך, יוצא בכל שנה; קודם שיתקשה, קרוי קור:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:11:4.english: The covering of a palm shoot - A fiber, like a patterned garment, [that] grows around the shoot of a date palm when it is tender. Kor — the branch of the tree when it is tender, [which] emerges each year; before it hardens, it is called kor.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:1:1.english: Every Shabbat day - Of all the Shabbats of the years.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:1:2.hebrew: הוה יתיב וגריס - שלא יקרב מלאך המות אליו, שהתורה מגינה ממות, כדאמרינן בסוטה (דף כא.):
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:1:2.english: He would sit and learn - So that the Angel of Death would not approach him, as the Torah protects from death, as we say in Sotah (21a).

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:1:3.hebrew: סליק ובחיש באילני - מנענע המלאך באילנות, להשמיע קול תימה:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:1:3.english: [He] climbed and shook the trees - The angel shook the trees, to make a strange sound.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:2:1.english: And the dogs of father’s house are hungry - He needed [to ask] both of these questions.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:2:2.hebrew: ולא יפה אמר כו' - שלתקנת הכלבים לא הצריכוהו לשנות טלטול נבילה, ואת האריה המת אסרו לטלטל אלא על ידי ככר או תינוק. ל"א: שהקדימוהו תשובת הכלב לתשובת האריה — לשון רבותי:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:2:2.english: And did [Solomon] not speak well, etc. - For, for the benefit of the dogs they did not require him to alter the handling of a carcass, whereas the dead lion they forbade to move except by means of a loaf or an infant. Another explanation: That they gave precedence to the response regarding the dog over the response regarding the lion — [this is] the wording of my teachers.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:2:3.english: And with regard to the question - Namely, whether it is permitted to extinguish [a lamp].

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:2:4.hebrew: דשאילנא קדמיכון - דרך ענוה אמר, דהוה ליה למימר: ״דשאילתון קדמי״:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:2:4.english: That I asked before you - He said [this] out of humility, for he should have said: “That you asked before me.”

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:2:5.english: Is called a lamp - [As it is written:] “The lamp of God is the soul of man” (Proverbs 20:27).

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:2:6.hebrew: מוטב תכבה נרו כו' - לאו מהכא יליף חלול שבת, דפיקוח נפש נפקא לן מ"וחי בהם" — ולא שימות בהם; אלא להטעימן הדבר באגדה המושכת את הלב, לפי שהיו באים לשמוע הדרשה נשים ועמי הארץ, והיו צריכין הדרשנין למשוך את לבבם:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:2:6.english: It is preferable that the lamp be extinguished, etc. - Not from here did he derive [the permissibility of] desecrating Shabbat, for [the principle of] saving a life is derived by us from “and live by them” — and not that he should die by them. Rather, [he said this] to give them a taste of the matter through Aggadah that captivates the heart, because women and unlearned people would come to hear the sermon, and the preachers needed to attract their hearts.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:3:1.hebrew: תחלתו וסופו - וכ"ש שיש עוד בינתיים:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:3:1.english: Its beginning and its end - And all the more so there are more [words of Torah] in between.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:3:2.hebrew: קודם השמש - אם יעמול בתורה שקדמה לשמש, יש יתרון:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:3:2.english: Before the sun - If he toils in the Torah, which preceded the sun, there is profit.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:3:3.english: To keep company - Companionship; in Old French: solaz.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:4:2.hebrew: משחוק שמשחק עם הרשעים - שנותן להם שעה משחקת, כדי להאכילן חלקן ולטורדן מן העולם הבא:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:4:2.english: Than the laughter which He laughs with the wicked - That He gives them an hour when fortune smiles, in order to feed them their portion and banish them from the World-to-Come.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:5:1.english: The joy of a mitzva - Such as escorting a bride [to the wedding canopy].

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:5:2.hebrew: שחוק - שחוק ממש, שאין דעת שוחק מיושבת עליו; ואפילו אינו של לצון, מ"מ אין בו יישוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:5:2.english: Laughter - Actual laughter, for the mind of one who laughs is not settled upon him; and even if it is not [done out of] mockery, nevertheless there is no composure in it.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:5:4.english: Bring me a minstrel - It is a mitzvah [in order] to cause the Divine Presence to rest upon him.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:5:5.english: For a matter of halakha - One must open with words of humor first.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:5:6.hebrew: לחלום טוב - אם בא לישן מתוך שמחה, מראין לו חלום טוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:5:6.english: For a good dream - If one goes to sleep out of joy, he is shown a good dream.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:6:1.english: Dripping with bitterness - Bitterness due to awe.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:6:2.english: And the Sages were cheered - Their hearts opened on account of the joy.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:8:1.english: From impudent people - That they should not harm me.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:8:2.hebrew: ומעזות פנים - שלא יצא עלי שם ממזרות, דהוא עז פנים:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:8:2.english: And from insolence - That a reputation of mamzerut should not emerge concerning me, for [a mamzer] is insolent.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:9:1.english: In matters of Torah - It is permitted to answer [him] according to his folly.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:9:2.hebrew: הרה ויולדת יחדיו - ביום שהרה זה, יולדת ולד אחר, כמו תרנגולת. וכיון שמשמשת בכל יום, נמצאת יולדת בכל יום, דהכי משמע קרא: בכל עת שהיא מתעברת — יולדת, שממהרת לגמור צורת הולד לזמן מועט:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:9:2.english: The woman with child and her that gives birth together - On the day she conceives this [child], she gives birth to another child, like a chicken. And since she engages in marital relations every day, she turns out to give birth every day, for this is what the verse means: Whenever she conceives, she gives birth, as [her body] quickly completes the formation of the fetus in a short time.

Rashi on Shabbat 30b:9:3.hebrew: בא ואראך - טרח לענותו כאולתו, כדי להעמיד דברי תורה על מכונו:
Rashi on Shabbat 30b:9:3.english: Come and I will show you - He took the trouble to answer him according to his folly, in order to establish the words of Torah on their [proper] foundation.
